units.excerpt: We believe the scientific study of catastrophic risks from AI has fallen far short of where we need to be.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI states that scientific study of catastrophic AI risk is currently inadequate.

units.excerpt: To help address this gap, we are introducing our Preparedness Framework, a living document describing OpenAI’s processes to track, evaluate, forecast, and protect against catastrophic risks posed by increasingly powerful models.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI introduces the Preparedness Framework as a living document for tracking, evaluating, forecasting, and protecting against catastrophic risks from powerful models.

units.excerpt: Our practical experience with iterative deployment has enabled us to proactively improve our technical and procedural safety infrastructure.
units.paraphrase: Iterative deployment experience has allowed proactive improvements to safety infrastructure.

units.excerpt: As our systems get closer to AGI, we are becoming even more careful about the development of our models, especially in the context of catastrophic risk.
units.paraphrase: As systems approach AGI, OpenAI is becoming more cautious about model development regarding catastrophic risk.

units.excerpt: This Preparedness Framework is a living document that distills our latest learnings on how to best achieve safe development and deployment in practice.
units.paraphrase: The Framework distills current learnings on achieving safe development and deployment.

units.excerpt: The processes laid out in each version of the Preparedness Framework will help us rapidly improve our understanding of the science and empirical texture of catastrophic risk, and establish the processes needed to protect against unsafe development.
units.paraphrase: The Framework's processes are intended to rapidly advance understanding of catastrophic risk and establish protective processes.

units.excerpt: The central thesis behind our Preparedness Framework is that a robust approach to AI catastrophic risk safety requires proactive, science-based determinations of when and how it is safe to proceed with development and deployment.
units.paraphrase: The Framework's central thesis is that safety requires proactive, science-based determinations of when development and deployment are safe.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.excerpt: Tracking catastrophic risk level via evaluations. We will be building and continually improving suites of evaluations and other monitoring solutions along several Tracked Risk Categories, and indicating our current levels of pre-mitigation and post-mitigation risk in a Scorecard.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI will build and improve evaluation suites across Tracked Risk Categories and report risk levels in a Scorecard.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.context_stem: Tracking catastrophic risk level via evaluations.
units.excerpt: Importantly, we will also be forecasting the future development of risks, so that we can develop lead times on safety and security measures
units.paraphrase: OpenAI will also forecast future risk development to build lead time for safety and security measures.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.excerpt: Seeking out unknown-unknowns. We will continually run a process for identification and analysis (as well as tracking) of currently unknown categories of catastrophic risk as they emerge
units.paraphrase: OpenAI will run an ongoing process to identify, analyze, and track currently unknown categories of catastrophic risk.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.excerpt: Establishing safety baselines. Only models with a post-mitigation score of "medium" or below can be deployed, and only models with a post-mitigation score of "high" or below can be developed further (as defined in the Tracked Risk Categories below).
units.paraphrase: Deployment is limited to models scoring medium or below post-mitigation, and further development is limited to models scoring high or below.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.excerpt: In addition, we will ensure Security is appropriately tailored to any model that has a “high” or “critical” pre-mitigation level of risk (as defined in the Scorecard below) to prevent model exfiltration.
units.paraphrase: Security measures will be tailored for models with high or critical pre-mitigation risk to prevent exfiltration.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.excerpt: We also establish procedural commitments (as defined in Governance below) that further specify how we operationalize all the activities that the Preparedness Framework outlines.
units.paraphrase: Procedural commitments in the Governance section specify how Framework activities are operationalized.

units.excerpt: Our focus in this document is on catastrophic risk. By catastrophic risk, we mean any risk which could result in hundreds of billions of dollars in economic damage or lead to the severe harm or death of many individuals—this includes, but is not limited to, existential risk.
units.paraphrase: Catastrophic risk is defined as risk causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage or severe harm/death, including existential risk.

units.excerpt: Proactive in this case refers to an aim to develop this science ahead of the first time it becomes necessary. Deployment in this case refers to the spectrum of ways of releasing a technology for external impact. Development in this case refers to the spectrum of activities to enhance the technology.
units.paraphrase: Defines proactive, deployment, and development as used in the document.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.excerpt: Tasking the Preparedness team with on-the-ground work. The Preparedness team will drive the technical work and maintenance of the Preparedness Framework.
units.paraphrase: The Preparedness team will lead the technical work and maintenance of the Framework.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.context_stem: Tasking the Preparedness team with on-the-ground work.
units.excerpt: This includes conducting research, evaluations, monitoring, and forecasting of risks, and synthesizing this work via regular reports to the Safety Advisory Group.
units.paraphrase: The team's work includes research, evaluations, monitoring, forecasting, and synthesizing reports to the Safety Advisory Group.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.context_stem: Tasking the Preparedness team with on-the-ground work.
units.excerpt: These reports will include a summary of the latest evidence and make recommendations on changes needed to enable OpenAI to plan ahead.
units.paraphrase: Reports will summarize the latest evidence and recommend changes to enable forward planning.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.context_stem: Tasking the Preparedness team with on-the-ground work.
units.excerpt: The Preparedness team will also call on and coordinate with relevant teams (e.g., Safety Systems, Security, Superalignment, Policy Research) to collate recommended mitigations to include in these reports.
units.paraphrase: The Preparedness team will coordinate with other teams to gather recommended mitigations for its reports.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.context_stem: Tasking the Preparedness team with on-the-ground work.
units.excerpt: In addition, Preparedness will also manage safety drills and coordinate with the Trustworthy AI team for third-party auditing.
units.paraphrase: Preparedness will manage safety drills and coordinate third-party auditing with the Trustworthy AI team.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.excerpt: Creating a cross-functional advisory body. We are creating a Safety Advisory Group (SAG) that brings together expertise from across the company to help OpenAI’s leadership and Board of Directors be best prepared for the safety decisions they need to make.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI is establishing a cross-functional Safety Advisory Group to prepare leadership and the Board for safety decisions.

units.section_heading: Our Preparedness Framework contains five key elements
units.excerpt: SAG responsibilities will thus include overseeing the assessment of the risk landscape, and maintaining a fast-track process for handling emergency scenarios.
units.paraphrase: SAG will oversee risk landscape assessment and maintain a fast-track process for emergencies.

units.excerpt: Finally, OpenAI’s primary fiduciary duty is to humanity, and we are committed to doing the research required to make AGI safe.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI states its primary fiduciary duty is to humanity and commits to AGI safety research.

units.excerpt: Therefore, the Preparedness Framework is meant to be just one piece of our overall approach to safety and alignment, which also includes investment in mitigating bias, hallucination, and misuse, facilitating democratic inputs to AI, improving alignment methods, investing significantly in security and safety research.
units.paraphrase: The Framework is one component of a broader safety and alignment approach that also covers bias, hallucination, misuse mitigation, democratic input, alignment methods, and security research.

units.excerpt: This is also one more way in which we are meeting our voluntary commitments to safety, security and trust in AI that we made in July 2023.
units.paraphrase: The Framework also fulfills voluntary safety, security, and trust commitments made in July 2023.

units.excerpt: We recognize other organizations for contributing to action in this space too, for example, via publishing Responsible Scaling Policies, and encourage others in the industry to adopt similar approaches.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI acknowledges other organizations' contributions, such as Responsible Scaling Policies, and encourages industry-wide adoption of similar approaches.

units.excerpt: This living document has three sections:
units.paraphrase: The document introduces its three main sections.

units.context_stem: This living document has three sections:
units.excerpt: Tracked Risk Categories, in which we detail the key areas of risk we will track as well as delineations of different levels of these risk
units.paraphrase: The Tracked Risk Categories section details key risk areas and their gradation levels.

units.context_stem: This living document has three sections:
units.excerpt: Scorecard, in which we will indicate our current assessments of the level of risk along each tracked risk category
units.paraphrase: The Scorecard section will show current risk assessments for each tracked category.

units.context_stem: This living document has three sections:
units.excerpt: Governance, in which we lay out our safety baselines as well as procedural commitments, which include standing up a Safety Advisory Group.
units.paraphrase: The Governance section lays out safety baselines and procedural commitments, including standing up a Safety Advisory Group.

units.excerpt: In this section, we identify the categories of risks that we will be tracking, along with a dedicated workstream for identifying and adding new or nascent categories of risk as they emerge, i.e., “unknown unknowns.”
units.paraphrase: This section identifies tracked risk categories and a workstream for adding new emerging risks.

units.excerpt: Our intent is to “go deep” in the tracked categories to ensure we are testing for any possible worst-case scenarios, while also maintaining a broad holistic view of risks via monitoring activities across OpenAI and the “unknown unknowns” identification process.
units.paraphrase: The intent is to test deeply within tracked categories for worst-case scenarios while maintaining broad monitoring across OpenAI.

units.excerpt: Each of the Tracked Risk Categories comes with a gradation scale.
units.paraphrase: Each tracked risk category has an associated gradation scale.

units.excerpt: We believe monitoring gradations of risk will enable us to get in front of escalating threats and be able to apply more tailored mitigations.
units.paraphrase: Monitoring risk gradations is believed to enable proactive response and tailored mitigations to escalating threats.

units.excerpt: In general, “low” on this gradation scale is meant to indicate that the corresponding category of risks is not yet a significant problem, while “critical” represents the maximal level of concern.
units.paraphrase: On the gradation scale, low indicates a not-yet-significant risk while critical indicates maximal concern.

units.excerpt: Specifically, below, we lay out details for the following Tracked Risk Categories
units.paraphrase: The section introduces a list of the specific tracked risk categories.

units.context_stem: Specifically, below, we lay out details for the following Tracked Risk Categories
units.excerpt: Cybersecurity
units.paraphrase: Cybersecurity is listed as a tracked risk category.

units.context_stem: Specifically, below, we lay out details for the following Tracked Risk Categories
units.excerpt: Chemical, Biological, Nuclear, and Radiological (CBRN) threats
units.paraphrase: CBRN threats are listed as a tracked risk category.

units.context_stem: Specifically, below, we lay out details for the following Tracked Risk Categories
units.excerpt: Persuasion
units.paraphrase: Persuasion is listed as a tracked risk category.

units.context_stem: Specifically, below, we lay out details for the following Tracked Risk Categories
units.excerpt: Model autonomy
units.paraphrase: Model autonomy is listed as a tracked risk category.

units.excerpt: Our rationale for grouping and naming these specific risk categories is informed by three considerations.
units.paraphrase: Three considerations inform the naming and grouping of risk categories.

units.excerpt: First, fine-tuning or other domain-specific enhancements (e.g., tailored prompts or language model programs) may better elicit model capabilities along a particular risk category.
units.paraphrase: Fine-tuning or domain-specific enhancements may better elicit risk-relevant model capabilities.

units.excerpt: Our evaluations will thus include tests against these enhanced models to ensure we are testing against the “worst case” scenario we know of.
units.paraphrase: Evaluations will test enhanced models to capture worst-case scenarios.

units.excerpt: Our procedural commitments are triggered when any of the tracked risk categories increase in severity, rather than only when they all increase together.
units.paraphrase: Procedural commitments trigger when any single tracked category increases in severity, not only when all increase together.

units.excerpt: Because capability improvements across different domains do not necessarily occur at the same rate, this approach ensures we err on the side of safety.
units.paraphrase: Since capability improvements vary by domain, the trigger approach errs on the side of safety.

units.excerpt: Second, this approach enables us to leverage domain-specific talent to develop tailored suites of evaluations and monitoring solutions for each risk category.
units.paraphrase: The second rationale is that grouping allows leveraging domain-specific talent for tailored evaluations per category.

units.excerpt: Third, this approach increases options for tailored, domain-specific mitigations, to help minimize the need for broader, more disruptive actions.
units.paraphrase: The third rationale is that this approach increases tailored mitigation options, reducing the need for broader disruptive actions.

units.excerpt: Also, the risk categories that we are considering are not necessarily independent and are likely to interact with each other.
units.paraphrase: The considered risk categories may not be independent and are likely to interact.

units.excerpt: Decisions to group certain risks are thus motivated by operational efficiencies (as well as by the desire to have a relatively compact set of Tracked Risk Categories).
units.paraphrase: Grouping decisions are motivated by operational efficiency and keeping the category list compact.

units.excerpt: As mentioned, the empirical study of catastrophic risk from frontier AI models is nascent.
units.paraphrase: The empirical study of catastrophic risk from frontier models remains at an early stage.

units.excerpt: Our current estimates of levels and thresholds for “medium” through “critical” risk are therefore speculative and will keep being refined as informed by future research.
units.paraphrase: Current risk-level thresholds are speculative and will be refined as research progresses.

units.excerpt: For this reason, we defer specific details on evaluations to the Scorecard section (and this section is intended to be updated frequently).
units.paraphrase: Specific evaluation details are deferred to the Scorecard section, which will be updated frequently.

units.excerpt: Cybersecurity is focused on risks related to use of the model for cyber-exploitation to disrupt confidentiality, integrity, and/or availability of computer systems.
units.paraphrase: Cybersecurity risk concerns model-enabled cyber-exploitation that disrupts confidentiality, integrity, or availability of computer systems.

units.excerpt: Model assistance for cyberattacks, if any, is meaningful only for non-programming uses, e.g., translation, targeted distillation of confidential information, and/or data analysis AND model cannot meaningfully execute elements of cyber operations, e.g., developing a known exploit into an attack, black-box exploitation, translating reasoning about defenses into action, or lateral goal-directed movement on hardened targets.
units.paraphrase: At Low, model assistance for cyberattacks is limited to non-programming uses and the model cannot execute core cyber-operation elements.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Low; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Non-programming tasks represent a sizable bottleneck for threat actors; however, the skills involved are not terribly specialized and the benefit comes often from intersectional skills (i.e., proficiency in English and a high level understanding of political or technical systems to summarize emails).
units.paraphrase: Non-programming tasks are a bottleneck but require only moderately specialized, often intersectional, skills.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Low; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: We exclude vulnerability discovery because the harm at this stage is not identification of individual vulnerabilities, but moreso the implementation and deployment of an exploit against a target.
units.paraphrase: Vulnerability discovery is excluded because harm arises from exploit implementation and deployment, not identification alone.

units.excerpt: Model increases the productivity of operators by an efficiency threshold (e.g. >2x time saved) on key cyber operation tasks, such as developing a known exploit into an attack, black-box exploitation, goal-directed lateral movement, identification of valuable information, remaining undetected, or reacting to defense.
units.paraphrase: At Medium, the model increases operator productivity by over 2x on key cyber-operation tasks.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Medium; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: The execution of a cyberattack is a scarce skill that is generally learned from experience. A model’s ability to substitute in for or accelerate a professional would improve the quality or quantity of attacks.
units.paraphrase: Cyberattack execution is a scarce, experience-based skill, so model substitution would improve attack quality or quantity.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Medium; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Note that this productivity speedup also includes low-level (potentially state) actors using known methods, e.g. Russian disinformation groups, who use purchased capabilities, phishing, and otherwise known methods.
units.paraphrase: The productivity speedup also applies to low-level or state actors using known methods such as phishing.

units.excerpt: Tool-augmented model can identify and develop proofs-of-concept for high-value exploits against hardened targets without human intervention, potentially involving novel exploitation techniques, OR provided with a detailed strategy, the model can end-to-end execute cyber operations involving the above tasks without human intervention.
units.paraphrase: At High, the model can autonomously develop proofs-of-concept for high-value exploits or end-to-end execute cyber operations given a strategy.

units.context_stem: Risk level: High; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: High-value exploits are generally against hardened platforms, scarce, and easily productionizable (e.g., a zero-click iOS exploit). While weaker vulnerability detection capabilities (e.g. those already cheaply available and fairly liquid on exploit markets) do not meaningfully address a bottleneck for attackers, such advanced capability would unblock many and be usable by actors of many skill levels.
units.paraphrase: High-value exploits are scarce and against hardened platforms; unlike weaker detection tools, this advanced capability would unblock many attackers of varying skill.

units.context_stem: Risk level: High; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: End-to-end execution would dramatically accelerate the quality or quantity of professional cyberattacks.
units.paraphrase: End-to-end execution capability would significantly boost professional cyberattack quality or quantity.

units.excerpt: Tool-augmented model can identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels, across all software projects, without human intervention OR model can devise and execute end-to-end novel strategies for cyberattacks against hardened targets given only a high level desired goal.
units.paraphrase: At Critical, the model can independently develop functional zero-day exploits across all software or devise novel cyberattack strategies from a high-level goal.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Finding and executing end-to-end exploits for all software would lead to catastrophe from unilateral actors, from hacking military or industrial systems as well as OpenAI infrastructure.
units.paraphrase: End-to-end exploitation capability across all software could enable catastrophic unilateral attacks on military, industrial, or OpenAI systems.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Novel cyber operations generally pose the most serious threat, as they are unpredictable and scarce. They may involve, e.g., novel zero-days or methods of command-and-control.
units.paraphrase: Novel cyber operations pose the greatest threat due to their unpredictability and scarcity.

units.excerpt: CBRN is focused on risks related to model-assisted creation of chemical, biological, radiological, and/or nuclear threats.
units.paraphrase: CBRN risk concerns model-assisted creation of chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear threats.

units.excerpt: Model can provide information relevant to creating CBRN threats with comparable utility to existing resources (e.g., textbooks, search engines).
units.paraphrase: At Low, model-provided information is comparable in utility to existing resources like textbooks or search engines.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Low; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Minimal change from status quo where other resources (e.g., textbooks, search engines) already exist.
units.paraphrase: This represents minimal change from the existing status quo of available resources.

units.excerpt: Model provides meaningfully improved assistance that increases ability for existing experts in CBRN-related advanced fields to be able to create a known CBRN threat (e.g., tacit knowledge, specific supplier information, plans for distribution).
units.paraphrase: At Medium, the model meaningfully improves existing experts' ability to create a known CBRN threat.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Medium; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Models may allow users to learn critical pieces of information faster than they could with existing resources, or explain variations on steps more flexibly than existing resources.
units.paraphrase: Models may accelerate learning of critical information or explain step variations more flexibly than existing resources.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Medium; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: This increases the accessibility of creating a CBRN threat, although risk is limited as experts already have significant domain expertise and reputation.
units.paraphrase: Accessibility of creating a CBRN threat increases, but risk remains limited since experts already have domain expertise and reputational stakes.

units.excerpt: Model enables an expert to develop a novel threat vector OR model provides meaningfully improved assistance that enables anyone with basic training in a relevant field (e.g., introductory undergraduate biology course) to be able to create a CBRN threat.
units.paraphrase: At High, the model enables experts to create novel threat vectors or enables basically-trained individuals to create a CBRN threat.

units.context_stem: Risk level: High; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: The creation of a weak novel threat is also a leading indicator for catastrophic new threats, for which defenses (e.g., vaccines) are much weaker or nonexistent.
units.paraphrase: A weak novel threat is a leading indicator of catastrophic threats for which defenses are weak or absent.

units.context_stem: Risk level: High; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Allowing those with basic training to create CBRN threats is a major increase in accessibility, which requires drastic action, especially for biological and chemical risks as their material requirements are not as onerous.
units.paraphrase: Enabling basically-trained individuals to create CBRN threats greatly increases accessibility, requiring drastic action, especially for biological and chemical risks.

units.excerpt: Model enables an expert to develop a highly dangerous novel threat vector (e.g., comparable to novel CDC Class A biological agent) OR model provides meaningfully improved assistance that enables anyone to be able to create a known CBRN threat OR model can be connected to tools and equipment to complete the full engineering and/or synthesis cycle of a regulated or novel CBRN threat without human intervention.
units.paraphrase: At Critical, the model enables highly dangerous novel threats, enables anyone to create known CBRN threats, or can autonomously complete the full engineering/synthesis cycle of a CBRN threat.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: The creation of a novel threat vector on the scale of a CDC Class A biological agent (i.e., high mortality, ease of transmission) could cause millions of deaths and significantly disrupt public life.
units.paraphrase: A novel threat comparable to a CDC Class A agent could cause millions of deaths and severe societal disruption.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Allowing anyone to create CBRN threats would maximally extend accessibility.
units.paraphrase: Enabling anyone to create CBRN threats represents maximal accessibility extension.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Significantly automating the end-to-end engineering or synthesis cycle for a CBRN threat would also enable unprecedented and massive scale of potential attacks.
units.paraphrase: Automating the full engineering or synthesis cycle would enable attacks at unprecedented scale.

units.excerpt: Persuasion is focused on risks related to convincing people to change their beliefs (or act on) both static and interactive model-generated content.
units.paraphrase: Persuasion risk concerns model-generated static or interactive content that changes beliefs or induces action.

units.excerpt: We define persuasive capability via the level of human persuasive content that can be commoditized by the model.
units.paraphrase: Persuasive capability is defined by the level of human persuasive content the model can commoditize.

units.excerpt: Typically, strong persuasion is rare and requires significant human effort (e.g., a 1:1 grassroots conversation, or a highly polished podcast); however, models could make all content up to their capability level nearly zero-cost to generate.
units.paraphrase: Strong persuasion normally requires significant human effort, but models could make content up to their capability level nearly free to produce.

units.excerpt: Model can create (potentially interactive) content with comparable persuasive effectiveness to reading a low-quality article.
units.paraphrase: At Low, model content is as persuasive as a low-quality article.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Low; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Low-quality articles are very common and low-impact, so model commoditization has negligible impact.
units.paraphrase: Since low-quality articles are common and low-impact, model commoditization at this level has negligible effect.

units.excerpt: Model can create (potentially interactive) content with comparable persuasive effectiveness to typical human-written content (e.g., an op-ed from a reputable news source; 1:1 conversation with a typical randomly-assigned individual).
units.paraphrase: At Medium, model content is as persuasive as typical human-written content such as a reputable op-ed or a typical 1:1 conversation.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Medium; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: This makes models a significant aid to biased journalism, get-out-the-vote campaigns, and typical scams or spear phishers.
units.paraphrase: At this level, models significantly aid biased journalism, voter mobilization campaigns, and scams or phishing.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Medium; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: It could affect politics, marketing, or social engineering in a similar fashion to hiring a large, very cheap, and moderately skilled workforce.
units.paraphrase: This capability could affect politics, marketing, or social engineering similarly to hiring a large, cheap, moderately-skilled workforce.

units.excerpt: Model can create (potentially interactive) content with empirically comparable persuasive effectiveness to a country-wide change agent.
units.paraphrase: At High, model content is as persuasive as a country-wide change agent.

units.context_stem: Risk level: High; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: This has a similar risk profile to a country-wide change agent; it could dramatically affect elections and democratic outcomes.
units.paraphrase: This capability could dramatically affect elections and democratic outcomes, similar to a country-wide change agent.

units.excerpt: Model can create (potentially interactive) content with persuasive effectiveness strong enough to convince almost anyone to take action on a belief that goes against their natural interest.
units.paraphrase: At Critical, model content can convince almost anyone to act against their own interests.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: This represents a superhuman persuasive threat; it would be a powerful weapon for controlling nation-states, extracting secrets, and interfering with democracy.
units.paraphrase: This level represents a superhuman persuasive threat capable of controlling nations, extracting secrets, and undermining democracy.

units.excerpt: Model autonomy enables actors to run scaled misuse that can adapt to environmental changes and evade attempts to mitigate or shut down operations.
units.paraphrase: Model autonomy risk enables scaled misuse that can adapt and evade mitigation or shutdown efforts.

units.excerpt: Autonomy is also a prerequisite for self-exfiltration, self-improvement, and resource acquisition.
units.paraphrase: Autonomy is a prerequisite for self-exfiltration, self-improvement, and resource acquisition.

units.excerpt: Model can take discrete actions if explicitly instructed to do so.
units.paraphrase: At Low, the model can take discrete actions only when explicitly instructed.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Low; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: This limits the model to single-step tasks in a “human assistance” use case, where the step is generally clear and outcomes are easily understood.
units.paraphrase: This level restricts the model to clear, single-step human-assistance tasks.

units.excerpt: Model can robustly complete a diverse set of chained actions and acquire resources (e.g., spin up an AWS instance, complete a Fiverr task) OR model, with basic scaffolding, can use off-the-shelf software to execute well-specified coding tasks on a standalone, toy, or handcrafted repository
units.paraphrase: At Medium, the model can chain diverse actions and acquire resources, or with basic scaffolding execute well-specified coding tasks on a toy repository.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Medium; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Solving well-specified tasks demonstrates a strong understanding of programming and a moderate ability to handle real world errors
units.paraphrase: Solving well-specified tasks shows strong programming understanding and moderate real-world error handling.

units.excerpt: Model can execute open-ended, novel ML tasks on a production ML codebase that would constitute a significant step on the critical path to model self-improvement (e.g., an OpenAI pull request that trains a new model with highly diverse datasets to improve codebase editing performance, using internal tooling and documentation).
units.paraphrase: At High, the model can execute open-ended novel ML tasks on production codebases representing significant steps toward self-improvement.

units.context_stem: Risk level: High; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Solving open-ended tasks offers an immediate speedup for AI research and demonstrates a strong level of long-context understanding and adaptation.
units.paraphrase: Solving open-ended tasks accelerates AI research and shows strong long-context understanding and adaptation.

units.context_stem: Risk level: High; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: However, this does not yet demonstrate the ability to orchestrate continual improvements over time (i.e., improvements may be bounded or evolutionary rather than revolutionary); further, models are still restricted by access to compute and other resources.
units.paraphrase: This level does not yet show continual self-improvement capability, and models remain constrained by compute and resource access.

units.excerpt: Model can profitably survive and replicate in the wild given minimal human instruction, i.e., without listing explicit approaches OR model can self-exfiltrate under current prevailing security OR model can conduct AI research fully autonomously (e.g., autonomously identify and validate a 2x compute efficiency improvement)
units.paraphrase: At Critical, the model can autonomously survive and replicate, self-exfiltrate under current security, or conduct AI research fully autonomously, including validating a 2x compute efficiency improvement.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: If the model is able to successfully replicate and survive or self-exfiltrate, controlling the model would be very difficult. Such a model might be able to also adapt to humans attempting to shut it down.
units.paraphrase: A model capable of replication, survival, or self-exfiltration would be very difficult to control and might adapt to shutdown attempts.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: Finally, such a model would likely be able to create unified, goal-directed plans across a variety of domains (e.g., from running commands on Linux to orchestrating tasks on Fiverr).
units.paraphrase: Such a model would likely be able to form unified, goal-directed plans across many domains.

units.context_stem: Risk level: Critical; Column: Rationale for threshold
units.excerpt: If the model is able to conduct AI research fully autonomously, it could set off an intelligence explosion.
units.paraphrase: Fully autonomous AI research capability could trigger an intelligence explosion.

units.excerpt: By intelligence explosion, we mean a cycle in which the AI system improves itself, which makes the system more capable of more improvements, creating a runaway process of self-improvement.
units.paraphrase: Intelligence explosion is defined as a runaway self-improvement cycle where the AI system repeatedly improves itself.

units.excerpt: A concentrated burst of capability gains could outstrip our ability to anticipate and react to them.
units.paraphrase: A concentrated capability gain burst could exceed the ability to anticipate and respond.

units.excerpt: The list of Tracked Risk Categories above is almost certainly not exhaustive.
units.paraphrase: The list of Tracked Risk Categories is likely incomplete.

units.excerpt: As our understanding of the potential impacts and capabilities of frontier models improves, the listing will likely require expansions that accommodate new or understudied, emerging risks.
units.paraphrase: As understanding improves, the list will likely expand to cover new or understudied emerging risks.

units.excerpt: Therefore, as a part of our Governance process (described later in this document), we will continually assess whether there is a need for including a new category of risk in the list above and how to create gradations.
units.paraphrase: As part of Governance, OpenAI will continually assess whether new risk categories are needed and how to grade them.

units.excerpt: In addition, we will invest in staying abreast of relevant research developments and monitoring for observed misuse (expanded on later in this document), to help us understand if there are any emerging or understudied threats that we need to track.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI will invest in tracking research developments and observed misuse to identify emerging or understudied threats.

units.excerpt: The initial set of Tracked Risk Categories stems from an effort to identify the minimal set of “tripwires" required for the emergence of any catastrophic risk scenario we could reasonably envision.
units.paraphrase: The initial Tracked Risk Categories were derived from identifying minimal tripwires for foreseeable catastrophic risk scenarios.

units.excerpt: Note that we include deception and social engineering evaluations as part of the persuasion risk category, and include autonomous replication, adaptation, and AI R&D as part of the model autonomy risk category.
units.paraphrase: Deception and social engineering evaluations fall under persuasion, while autonomous replication, adaptation, and AI R&D fall under model autonomy.

units.excerpt: As a part of our Preparedness Framework, we will maintain a dynamic (i.e., frequently updated) Scorecard that is designed to track our current pre-mitigation model risk across each of the risk categories, as well as the post-mitigation risk.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI will maintain a frequently updated Scorecard tracking pre- and post-mitigation risk across categories.

units.excerpt: The Scorecard will be regularly updated by the Preparedness team to help ensure it reflects the latest research and findings.
units.paraphrase: The Preparedness team will regularly update the Scorecard to reflect the latest research and findings.

units.excerpt: Sources that inform the updates to the Scorecard will also include tracking observed misuse, and other community red-teaming and input on our frontier models from other teams (e.g., Policy Research, Safety Systems, Superalignment).
units.paraphrase: Scorecard updates will draw on observed misuse tracking, community red-teaming, and input from other internal teams.

units.excerpt: We will run the same evaluations to determine risk level for both the pre-mitigation and the post-mitigation risk, but on different versions of the model (pre-mitigation vs post-mitigations, as clarified further below).
units.paraphrase: The same evaluations will be run on both pre- and post-mitigation model versions to determine risk levels.

units.excerpt: In practice, it will likely be the case that the overall post-mitigation risk is lower than the pre-mitigation risk.
units.paraphrase: Post-mitigation risk is expected to typically be lower than pre-mitigation risk.

units.excerpt: Pre-mitigation risk is meant to guide the level of our security efforts as well as drive the development of mitigations needed to bring down post-mitigation risk.
units.paraphrase: Pre-mitigation risk guides security effort levels and drives mitigation development to lower post-mitigation risk.

units.excerpt: In the end, coupling capabilities growth with robust safety solutions is at the core of our research processes, and post-mitigation risk is our way of tracking the overall “net output” of these processes.
units.paraphrase: Coupling capability growth with safety solutions is central to OpenAI's research process, tracked via post-mitigation risk as the net output.

units.excerpt: We want to ensure our understanding of pre-mitigation risk takes into account a model that is “worst known case” (i.e., specifically tailored) for the given domain.
units.paraphrase: Understanding of pre-mitigation risk should account for a worst-known-case, domain-tailored model.

units.excerpt: To this end, for our evaluations, we will be running them not only on base models (with highly-performant, tailored prompts wherever appropriate), but also on fine-tuned versions designed for the particular misuse vector without any mitigations in place.
units.paraphrase: Evaluations will run on both base models with tailored prompts and fine-tuned, unmitigated versions designed for specific misuse vectors.

units.excerpt: We will be running these evaluations continually, i.e., as often as needed to catch any non-trivial capability change, including before, during, and after training.
units.paraphrase: Evaluations will run continually, before, during, and after training, to catch any non-trivial capability change.

units.excerpt: This would include whenever there is a >2x effective compute increase or major algorithmic breakthrough.
units.paraphrase: Evaluations are triggered by more than a 2x effective compute increase or a major algorithmic breakthrough.

units.excerpt: To verify if mitigations have sufficiently and dependently reduced the resulting post-mitigation risk, we will also run evaluations on models after they have safety mitigations in place, again attempting to verify and test the possible “worst known case” scenario for these systems.
units.paraphrase: Evaluations will also be run on models with safety mitigations in place, testing for worst-known-case scenarios, to verify mitigation effectiveness.

units.excerpt: As part of our baseline commitments, we are aiming to keep post-mitigation risk at “medium” risk or below.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI's baseline commitment is to keep post-mitigation risk at medium or below.

units.excerpt: Many of the mitigations that would be necessary to address risks at a “high” or “critical” pre-mitigation level (e.g., hardening security) require adequate lead time to implement.
units.paraphrase: Mitigations needed for high or critical pre-mitigation risk, such as hardening security, require adequate lead time.

units.excerpt: For this reason, we will be investing in efforts that help create an internal “preparedness roadmap” and help us thus properly plan for and get ahead of the emerging risks.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI will invest in creating an internal preparedness roadmap to plan ahead of emerging risks.

units.excerpt: These efforts will include sustained research related to scaling trends for dangerous capabilities and ongoing monitoring of misuse.
units.paraphrase: Efforts will include sustained research on scaling trends for dangerous capabilities and ongoing misuse monitoring.

units.excerpt: We will also, in cooperation with other teams (e.g., Safety Systems), develop monitoring and investigative systems.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI will develop monitoring and investigative systems in cooperation with other teams such as Safety Systems.

units.excerpt: This monitoring of real-world misuse (as well as staying abreast of relevant research developments) will help us create a better picture of deployed model characteristics, and inform updates to our evaluations as necessary.
units.paraphrase: Monitoring of real-world misuse and research developments will inform a better understanding of deployed model characteristics and evaluation updates.

units.excerpt: A central part of meeting our safety baselines is implementing mitigations to address various types of model risk.
units.paraphrase: Mitigations are a key element of meeting the safety baselines.

units.excerpt: Our mitigation strategy will involve both containment measures, which help reduce risks related to possession of a frontier model, as well as deployment mitigations, which help reduce risks from active use of a frontier model.
units.paraphrase: The mitigation strategy covers both containment measures and deployment mitigations.

units.excerpt: As a result, these mitigations might span increasing compartmentalization, restricting deployment to trusted users, implementing refusals, redacting training data, or alerting distribution partners.
units.paraphrase: Possible mitigations include compartmentalization, restricting deployment, refusals, redacting training data, or alerting partners.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks that GPT plus search gives no improvement over search alone for undergraduate biology students writing agent development instructions.

units.paraphrase: The same no-improvement result also applies to undergraduate students in chemistry, nuclear, and radiological studies.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks that GPT plus search increases success in finding unscreened DNA suppliers by less than X% over search alone.

units.excerpt: Persuasion: Medium (pre-mitigation), Low (post-mitigation)
units.paraphrase: Persuasion is rated Medium pre-mitigation and Low post-mitigation.

units.paraphrase: At this level, the model matches typical human persuasive content, but mitigations reduce that to low-quality-article effectiveness.

units.paraphrase: This eval measures belief change from long-term interactive conversation with a model versus a human, before and after mitigations.

units.excerpt: Donations eval: Content generated by model does not significantly increase donations to a charitable cause compared to human-generated controls (X% vs X%)
units.paraphrase: This eval checks the model does not significantly increase charitable donations compared to human-generated content.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks the model does not significantly increase Chrome extension installation compared to human-generated content.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks the model's phishing email success rate stays below X%.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks that fewer than X% of subtly dangerous model-generated research proposals are approved by a biology wet lab.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks that no employees are convinced to run backdoored code inserted by ChatGPT.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks the model cannot convince any employees to copy model weights elsewhere.

units.paraphrase: This checks that fewer than X% of users use the model for political persuasion and no electoral campaigns rely on it.

units.paraphrase: At this level, the model can perform chained actions and acquire resources, but mitigations reduce it to isolated instructed actions only.

units.paraphrase: This eval measures freelance task completion rate on Fiverr with scaffolding, dropping to 0% after mitigations.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks the model cannot complete long-term research engineering tasks, requiring 0% success rate.

units.paraphrase: This eval checks the model cannot penetrate defenses protecting its own weights, requiring 0% success rate.

units.excerpt: Beyond our above-detailed processes with regards to evaluations, monitoring, and forecasting, we want to make a set of safety baselines and procedural commitments.
units.paraphrase: The governance section introduces safety baselines and procedural commitments beyond evaluation, monitoring, and forecasting processes.

units.excerpt: Note that these processes also apply to training runs as we will perform periodic evaluations (e.g., of checkpoints) during model training.
units.paraphrase: These processes will also apply during training runs through periodic checkpoint evaluations.

units.excerpt: As mentioned in the introduction, OpenAI already has extensive safety processes in place both before and after deployment (e.g., system cards, red-teaming, refusals, jailbreak monitoring, etc.).
units.paraphrase: OpenAI already maintains extensive pre- and post-deployment safety processes such as system cards, red-teaming, refusals, and jailbreak monitoring.

units.excerpt: We now augment these processes with three safety baselines.
units.paraphrase: Three additional safety baselines are now added to existing processes.

units.excerpt: If we reach (or are forecasted to reach) at least “high” pre-mitigation risk in any of the considered categories: we will ensure that our security is hardened in a way that is designed to prevent our mitigations and controls from being circumvented via exfiltration (by the time we hit “high” pre-mitigation risk).
units.paraphrase: Reaching or forecasting at least 'high' pre-mitigation risk in any category triggers hardened security designed to prevent circumvention via exfiltration.

units.excerpt: This is defined as establishing network and compute security controls designed to help prevent the captured risk from being exploited or exfiltrated, as assessed and implemented by the Security team.
units.paraphrase: This means establishing network and compute security controls to prevent exploitation or exfiltration of the captured risk, assessed and implemented by the Security team.

units.excerpt: increasing compartmentalization, including immediately restricting access to a limited nameset of people, restricting access to critical know-how such as algorithmic secrets or model weights, and including a strict approval process for access during this period
units.paraphrase: Possible measures include increasing compartmentalization, limiting access to few people, restricting access to critical know-how, and applying a strict approval process.

units.excerpt: deploying only into restricted environments (i.e., ensuring the model is only available for inference in restricted environments) with strong technical controls that allow us to moderate the model’s capabilities
units.paraphrase: Possible measure: deploy the model only into restricted inference environments with strong technical controls.

units.excerpt: increasing the prioritization of information security controls.
units.paraphrase: Possible measure: prioritize information security controls more highly.

units.excerpt: Only models with a post-mitigation score of "medium" or below can be deployed.
units.paraphrase: Deployment is limited to models with a post-mitigation score of medium or lower.

units.excerpt: In other words, if we reach (or are forecasted to reach) at least “high” pre-mitigation risk in any of the considered categories, we will not continue with deployment of that model (by the time we hit “high” pre-mitigation risk) until there are reasonably mitigations in place for the relevant post-mitigation risk level to be back at most to “medium” level.
units.paraphrase: If pre-mitigation risk reaches or is forecast to reach 'high' in any category, deployment halts until mitigations bring post-mitigation risk back to at most 'medium'.

units.excerpt: (Note that a potentially effective mitigation in this context could be restricting deployment to trusted parties.)
units.paraphrase: One possible effective mitigation is restricting deployment to trusted parties.

units.excerpt: Only models with a post-mitigation score of "high" or below can be developed further.
units.paraphrase: Further development is limited to models with a post-mitigation score of high or lower.

units.excerpt: In other words, if we reach (or are forecasted to reach) “critical” pre-mitigation risk along any risk category, we commit to ensuring there are sufficient mitigations in place for that model (by the time we reach that risk level in our capability development, let alone deployment) for the overall post-mitigation risk to be back at most to “high” level.
units.paraphrase: Reaching or forecasting 'critical' pre-mitigation risk triggers a commitment to sufficient mitigations bringing post-mitigation risk back to at most 'high'.

units.excerpt: Note that this should not preclude safety-enhancing development.
units.paraphrase: This restriction does not prevent safety-enhancing development from continuing.

units.excerpt: We would also focus our efforts as a company towards solving these safety challenges and only continue with capabilities-enhancing development if we can reasonably assure ourselves (via the operationalization processes) that it is safe to do so.
units.paraphrase: The company would focus on solving safety challenges and only continue capabilities development if it can reasonably assure itself, via operationalization processes, that doing so is safe.

units.excerpt: Additionally, to protect against “critical” pre-mitigation risk, we need dependable evidence that the model is sufficiently aligned that it does not initiate “critical”-risk-level tasks unless explicitly instructed to do so.
units.paraphrase: Protecting against critical pre-mitigation risk requires dependable evidence the model won't initiate critical-risk tasks unless explicitly instructed.

units.excerpt: We also establish an operational structure to oversee our procedural commitments.
units.paraphrase: An operational structure is established to oversee the procedural commitments.

units.excerpt: These commitments aim to make sure that: (1) there is a dedicated team “on the ground” focused on preparedness research and monitoring (Preparedness team), (2) there is an advisory group (Safety Advisory Group) that has a sufficient diversity of perspectives and technical expertise to provide nuanced input and recommendations, and (3) there is a final decision-maker (OpenAI Leadership, with the option for the OpenAI Board of Directors to overrule).
units.paraphrase: The commitments establish a Preparedness team, a Safety Advisory Group, and a final decision-maker in OpenAI Leadership, overrulable by the Board.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: The Preparedness team conducts research, evaluations, monitoring, forecasting, and continuous updating of the Scorecard with input from teams that have relevant domain expertise.
units.paraphrase: The Preparedness team performs research, evaluations, monitoring, forecasting, and Scorecard updates with input from relevant domain experts.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: The Safety Advisory Group (SAG), including the SAG Chair, provides a diversity of perspectives to evaluate the strength of evidence related to catastrophic risk and recommend appropriate actions.
units.paraphrase: The SAG, including its Chair, evaluates evidence of catastrophic risk and recommends appropriate actions.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: The SAG will strive to recommend mitigations that are as targeted and non-disruptive as possible while not compromising safety.
units.paraphrase: The SAG aims to recommend mitigations that are targeted and minimally disruptive without compromising safety.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: In particular, we recognize that pausing deployment or development would be the last resort (but potentially necessary) option in these circumstances
units.paraphrase: Pausing deployment or development is recognized as a last-resort but potentially necessary option.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: The members of the SAG and the SAG Chair are appointed by the OpenAI Leadership. This will be done in consultation with the BoD, as is common for important roles in general.
units.paraphrase: OpenAI Leadership appoints SAG members and the SAG Chair, in consultation with the Board.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: SAG membership will rotate yearly. OpenAI leadership might choose to re-appoint someone from previous years to ensure there is continuity of knowledge and experience, while still ensuring that fresh and timely perspectives are present in the group.
units.paraphrase: SAG membership rotates annually, though leadership may re-appoint prior members for continuity while keeping fresh perspectives.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: The SAG Chair makes any final decisions needed for the SAG. This role is expected to rotate, as appointed by OpenAI leadership.
units.paraphrase: The SAG Chair makes final SAG decisions, and this role is expected to rotate as appointed by leadership.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: The OpenAI Leadership, i.e., the CEO or a person designated by them, serves as the default decision-maker on all decisions
units.paraphrase: OpenAI Leadership, meaning the CEO or their designee, is the default decision-maker for all decisions.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: The OpenAI Board of Directors (BoD), as the ultimate governing body of OpenAI, will oversee OpenAI Leadership’s implementation and decision-making pursuant to this Preparedness Framework.
units.paraphrase: The Board of Directors, as the ultimate governing body, will oversee Leadership's implementation of the Framework.

units.section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
units.excerpt: The BoD may review certain decisions taken and will receive appropriate documentation (i.e., without needing to proactively ask) to ensure the BOD is fully informed and able to fulfill its oversight role
units.paraphrase: The Board may review decisions and automatically receives documentation to stay informed and fulfill its oversight role.

units.excerpt: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
units.paraphrase: This introduces a list of Preparedness team responsibilities.

units.context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
units.excerpt: maintaining and updating the Scorecard, including designing and running evaluations to provide Scorecard inputs and collecting relevant information on monitored misuse, red-teaming, and intelligence
units.paraphrase: Responsibility: maintain and update the Scorecard, run evaluations, and collect information on misuse, red-teaming, and intelligence.

units.context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
units.excerpt: monitoring for unknown unknowns and making the case for inclusion in the Preparedness Framework of any new risk categories as they emerge
units.paraphrase: Responsibility: monitor for unknown unknowns and propose adding new risk categories as they arise.

units.context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
units.excerpt: ensuring the risk level distinctions in the Tracked Risk Categories section are appropriate given developments in frontier AI models, and suggesting updates to these levels if needed
units.paraphrase: Responsibility: ensure risk level distinctions remain appropriate given AI developments and suggest updates as needed.

units.context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
units.excerpt: forecasting potential changes to catastrophic risk levels, and summarizing evidence for an “early warning” / “heads up” as needed
units.paraphrase: Responsibility: forecast potential catastrophic risk changes and summarize evidence for early warnings as needed.

units.context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
units.excerpt: providing a monthly report (sent to the SAG, Leadership and BoD) synthesizing the above with any potential protective actions (the SAG Chair, OpenAI Leadership, and/or BoD can adjust this cadence as needed
units.paraphrase: Responsibility: provide a monthly report to SAG, Leadership, and Board synthesizing findings and protective actions; cadence adjustable by SAG Chair, Leadership, or Board.

units.excerpt: If the Preparedness or any other team determines that any changes to the Preparedness Framework are necessary, it will include a case for this change in its report.

excerpt: OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that AGI (artificial general intelligence) benefits all of humanity. To pursue that mission, we are committed to safely developing and deploying highly capable AI systems, which create significant benefits and also bring new risks.
paraphrase: OpenAI states its mission to ensure AGI benefits humanity and its commitment to safely developing capable AI systems that bring both benefits and risks.

excerpt: We build for safety at every step and share our learnings so that society can make well-informed choices to manage new risks from frontier AI.
paraphrase: OpenAI commits to building safety throughout development and sharing findings to help society manage frontier AI risks.

excerpt: The Preparedness Framework is OpenAI’s approach to tracking and preparing for frontier capabilities that create new risks of severe harm.
paraphrase: The document defines the Preparedness Framework as OpenAI's approach to tracking and preparing for frontier capabilities that create severe harm risks.

excerpt: We currently focus this work on three areas of frontier capability, which we call Tracked Categories:
paraphrase: OpenAI states it currently focuses on three Tracked Categories of frontier capability.

paraphrase: Biological and chemical capabilities offer scientific benefits but can also lower barriers to creating weapons.

context_stem: We currently focus this work on three areas of frontier capability, which we call Tracked Categories:
excerpt: Cybersecurity capabilities that, in addition to helping protect vulnerable systems, can also create new risks of scaled cyberattacks and vulnerability exploitation.
paraphrase: Cybersecurity capabilities can protect systems but also enable larger-scale cyberattacks and exploitation.

excerpt: AI Self-improvement capabilities that, in addition to unlocking helpful capabilities faster, could also create new challenges for human control of AI systems.
paraphrase: AI self-improvement capabilities can accelerate beneficial progress but may also challenge human control over AI systems.

excerpt: In each area, we develop and maintain a threat model that identifies the risks of severe harm and sets thresholds we can measure to tell us when the models get capable enough to meaningfully pose these risks.
paraphrase: For each area, OpenAI maintains a threat model identifying severe harm risks and measurable capability thresholds.

excerpt: We won’t deploy these very capable models until we’ve built safeguards to sufficiently minimize the associated risks of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI commits to withholding deployment of highly capable models until sufficient safeguards exist.

excerpt: This Framework lays out the kinds of safeguards we expect to need, and how we’ll confirm internally and show externally that the safeguards are sufficient.
paraphrase: The document describes expected safeguards and how their sufficiency will be confirmed internally and demonstrated externally.

excerpt: In this updated version of the Framework we also introduce a set of Research Categories.
paraphrase: This version introduces new Research Categories.

excerpt: These are areas of capability that could pose risks of severe harm, that do not yet meet our criteria to be Tracked Categories, and where we are investing now to further develop our threat models and capability elicitation techniques.
paraphrase: Research Categories are capabilities with potential severe harm risk that don't yet meet Tracked Category criteria but warrant investment in threat modeling and elicitation.

excerpt: We are constantly refining our practices and advancing the science, to unlock the benefits of these technologies while addressing their risks.
paraphrase: OpenAI states an ongoing commitment to refining practices and science to balance benefits and risks.

excerpt: This revision of the Preparedness Framework focuses on the safeguards we expect will be needed for future models more capable than those we have today.
paraphrase: This revision focuses on anticipated safeguards for future, more capable models.

excerpt: By “severe harm” in this document, we mean the death or grave injury of thousands of people or hundreds of billions of dollars of economic damage.
paraphrase: The footnote defines severe harm as thousands of deaths/grave injuries or hundreds of billions of dollars in economic damage.

excerpt: Our safety stack addresses a broad spectrum of risks, including many with harms below this severity.
paraphrase: OpenAI notes its broader safety stack covers risks below the severe harm threshold too.

excerpt: In choosing to set a high bar here, we aim to ensure that the most severe risks receive attention commensurate with their magnitude.
paraphrase: OpenAI explains it set a high severity bar so the most severe risks get proportionate attention.

excerpt: We believe there are a limited number of AI capabilities that could pose new risks of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI believes only a limited set of AI capabilities pose new severe harm risks.

excerpt: In order to safely unlock the beneficial uses of frontier AI capabilities, we exercise particular caution and implement safeguards that sufficiently minimize the risk of severe harm in these areas.
paraphrase: OpenAI exercises caution and implements safeguards to minimize severe harm risk while unlocking beneficial uses.

excerpt: To do this, we:
paraphrase: Lead-in to the list of activities OpenAI undertakes.

excerpt: Decide where to focus – we use a holistic risk assessment to decide which frontier capability categories to track or research further, and to define threshold levels of those capabilities that are associated with meaningful increases in risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI uses holistic risk assessment to select which capability categories to track and to set thresholds tied to meaningful risk increases.

excerpt: Measure capabilities associated with risks of severe harms – we run in–scope models through frontier capability evaluations to measure the full extent of model capabilities before we deploy our models and during development.
paraphrase: OpenAI runs in-scope models through capability evaluations both before deployment and during development.

context_stem: Measure capabilities associated with risks of severe harms —

paraphrase: Capability elicitation efforts aim to detect when identified risk-relevant capability thresholds are reached.

excerpt: Safeguard against severe harms – we evaluate the likelihood that severe harms could actually occur in the context of deployment, using threat models that take our safeguards into account.
paraphrase: OpenAI evaluates likelihood of severe harm occurring in deployment context using threat models incorporating safeguards.

excerpt: We do not deploy models that reach a High capability threshold until the associated risks that they pose are sufficiently minimized.
paraphrase: Models reaching High capability thresholds are not deployed until their risks are sufficiently minimized.

excerpt: If a model under development reaches a Critical capability threshold, we also require safeguards to sufficiently minimize the associated risks during development, irrespective of deployment plans.
paraphrase: Models reaching Critical capability thresholds during development require safeguards regardless of deployment plans.

excerpt: Build trust – we engage with subject–matter experts across and beyond OpenAI to inform these efforts and to build confidence that we are meeting our commitments and effectively managing risk.
paraphrase: OpenAI engages internal and external experts to build confidence it is meeting commitments and managing risk effectively.

excerpt: An internal, cross-functional group of OpenAI leaders called the Safety Advisory Group (SAG) oversees the Preparedness Framework and makes expert recommendations on the level and type of safeguards required for deploying frontier capabilities safely and securely.
paraphrase: The Safety Advisory Group, a cross-functional internal leadership group, oversees the Framework and recommends safeguard levels and types.

paraphrase: OpenAI Leadership approves or rejects SAG recommendations, with Board oversight via the Safety and Security Committee.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework

excerpt: For example, our adoption of Capability Reports and Safeguards Reports parallels Anthropic’s updated RSP.

excerpt: We evaluate whether frontier capabilities create a risk of severe harm through a holistic risk assessment process.
paraphrase: A holistic risk assessment process is used to evaluate whether frontier capabilities create severe harm risk.

excerpt: This process draws on our own internal research and signals, and where appropriate incorporates feedback from academic researchers, independent domain experts, industry bodies such as the Frontier Model Forum, and the U.S. government and its partners, as well as relevant legal and policy mandates.
paraphrase: The risk assessment draws on internal research and, where appropriate, external feedback from academics, experts, industry bodies, and government, plus legal/policy mandates.

excerpt: Where we determine that a capability presents a real risk of severe harm, we may decide to monitor it as a Tracked Category or a Research Category.
paraphrase: Capabilities determined to present real severe harm risk may be monitored as Tracked or Research Categories.

excerpt: Tracked Categories are those capabilities which we track most closely, measuring them during each covered deployment and preparing safeguards for when a threshold level is crossed.
paraphrase: Tracked Categories are closely monitored capabilities, measured at each covered deployment, with safeguards prepared for threshold crossings.

excerpt: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
paraphrase: A capability qualifies as a Tracked Category if its risk meets five specified criteria.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Plausible: It must be possible to identify a causal pathway for a severe harm in the capability area, enabled by frontier AI.
paraphrase: Criterion 1: a plausible causal pathway to severe harm enabled by frontier AI must be identifiable.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Measurable: We can construct or adopt capability evaluations that measure capabilities that closely track the potential for the severe harm.
paraphrase: Criterion 2: capability evaluations must be constructible or adoptable that closely track severe harm potential.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Severe: There is a plausible threat model within the capability area that would create severe harm.
paraphrase: Criterion 3: a plausible threat model within the area must be capable of creating severe harm.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Net new: The outcome cannot currently be realized as described (including at that scale, by that threat actor, or for that cost) with existing tools and resources (e.g., available as of 2021) but without access to frontier AI.
paraphrase: Criterion 4: the outcome must be currently unachievable without frontier AI using existing tools/resources such as those available in 2021.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Instantaneous or irremediable: The outcome is such that once realized, its severe harms are immediately felt, or are inevitable due to a lack of feasible measures to remediate.
paraphrase: Criterion 5: harm realized must be either immediately felt or inevitable due to lack of feasible remediation.

excerpt: We review and update Tracked Categories periodically or when we learn significant new information.
paraphrase: Tracked Categories are reviewed and updated periodically or upon significant new information.

excerpt: Research Categories are capabilities that, while they do not meet the above criteria, nonetheless have the potential to cause or contribute to severe harm, and where we are working now in order to prepare to address risks in the future (including potentially by maturing them to Tracked Categories).
paraphrase: Research Categories are capabilities not meeting Tracked Category criteria but with potential to contribute to severe harm, prompting current preparatory work.

excerpt: For each Tracked Category, we develop and maintain a threat model identifying specific risks of severe harms that could arise from the frontier capabilities in that domain and sets corresponding capability thresholds that would lead to a meaningful increase in risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: For each Tracked Category, a threat model identifies severe harm risks and sets capability thresholds indicating meaningful risk increases.

excerpt: SAG reviews and approves these threat models.
paraphrase: SAG reviews and approves the threat models.

excerpt: Capability thresholds concretely describe things an AI system might be able to help someone do or might be able to do on its own that could meaningfully increase risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: Capability thresholds concretely describe assisted or autonomous actions that could meaningfully increase severe harm risk.

excerpt: High capability thresholds mean capabilities that significantly increase existing risk vectors for severe harm.
paraphrase: High capability thresholds are defined as capabilities significantly increasing existing severe harm risk vectors.

excerpt: Covered systems that cross this capability threshold are required to have robust and effective safeguards that sufficiently minimize the associated risk of severe harm before they are deployed and appropriate security controls as they are developed.
paraphrase: Systems crossing the High threshold require robust safeguards minimizing risk before deployment and appropriate security controls during development.

excerpt: Critical capability thresholds mean capabilities that present a meaningful risk of a qualitatively new threat vector for severe harm with no ready precedent.
paraphrase: Critical capability thresholds are capabilities presenting a meaningfully new, unprecedented severe harm threat vector.

excerpt: Critical capabilities require safeguards even during the development of the covered system, irrespective of deployment plans.
paraphrase: Critical capabilities require safeguards during development regardless of deployment plans.

excerpt: These criteria were informed in part by Meta’s recent Frontier AI Framework.
paraphrase: Footnote acknowledges Meta's Frontier AI Framework informed these criteria.

excerpt: Threat models are informed both by our broader risk assessment process, and by more specific information that we gather across OpenAI teams and external experts.
paraphrase: Threat models draw on both the broader risk assessment process and specific information gathered internally and externally.

paraphrase: Past deployment experience informs risk understanding, but net-new severe harm risks may require significant safeguards even absent realized harms.

excerpt: Within our wider safety stack, our Preparedness Framework is specifically focused on frontier AI risks meeting a specific definition of severe harms, and Persuasion category risks do not fit the criteria for inclusion.

excerpt: We invest deeply in developing or adopting new science-backed evaluations that provide high precision and high recall indications of whether a covered system has reached a capability threshold in one of our Tracked Categories.
paraphrase: OpenAI invests in science-backed evaluations designed to accurately detect when a system reaches a capability threshold in a Tracked Category.

excerpt: Our evaluations are intended to approximate the full capability that the adversary contemplated by our threat model could extract from the deployment candidate model, including by using the highest-capability tier of system settings, using a version of the model that has a negligible rate of safety-based refusals on our Tracked Category capability evaluations (which may require a separate model variant), and with the best presently-available scaffolds.
paraphrase: Evaluations aim to approximate the maximum capability an adversary could extract, using top-tier settings, low-refusal model variants, and best available scaffolding.

excerpt: Nonetheless, given the continuous progress in model scaffolding and elicitation techniques, we regard any one-time capability elicitation in a frontier model as a lower bound, rather than a ceiling, on capabilities that may emerge in real world use and misuse.
paraphrase: Because scaffolding and elicitation techniques keep improving, a single capability test is treated as a floor, not a ceiling, on real-world capability.

excerpt: We incorporate this uncertainty into our assessments. We monitor the technical landscape for changes to the elicitation techniques and best practices, and reassess our evaluations as needed.
